key_insight: An on-site dephased ensemble of local static solutions can reproduce the frequency-dependent local self-energy and persistent local moments of strongly correlated Mott insulators, closely matching DMFT.
engineering_relevance: This offers a computationally cheaper first-principles route for modeling paramagnetic Mott systems without large supercells or expensive quantum Monte Carlo solvers.
method: Build a thermal ensemble over all accessible local static electronic solutions on each site.
Average the local states to restore the paramagnetic, symmetry-unbroken description.
Extract a strong, DMFT-like frequency-dependent local self-energy from the ensemble.
evidence_signal: The abstract states that the DE approximation reproduces key Mott-insulator signatures and local moment dynamics in quantitative agreement with DMFT.
watch_item: The approach is local and ensemble-based, so its accuracy may depend on how completely the accessible local configurations are sampled and may be less reliable for nonlocal correlation effects.
paper_title: Strong correlations and local self-energies from on-site ensembles
